what_this_is: The complete section 44 matrix on the sparse-MoE hybrid Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and it is NOT A SCORABLE RESULT. It is kept because it is the reason a guard exists. The exact-locality gate requires bit-identical greedy replay; on this checkpoint two UNHOOKED control runs diverge at token 1, so the gate cannot attribute a candidate/control difference to the candidate. correctness.runtime_reproducible records that, output_identical is null (inconclusive) rather than false (an accusation), and decide.py refuses it while saying it is not the candidate's fault. RecurLocal is not the cause: on the dense checkpoint the same binary with the same policy gives control, control and candidate bit-identical.

provenance.note: sparse-MoE hybrid Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on the same pinned SparkInfer commit, hook and box as the dense matrix. SPARKINFER_PACKED_MAX_ROWS=8 on BOTH arms so the runtime actually batches. NOTE the exact-locality gate is INCONCLUSIVE on this checkpoint: two unhooked control runs diverge at token 2 and SPARKINFER_DETERMINISTIC=1 does not fix it, so a candidate/control difference cannot be attributed to the candidate. On the dense checkpoint the same binary and policy are bit-identical across control, control and candidate.

correctness.method: greedy replay, token-exact -- INCONCLUSIVE: two control runs of this runtime on this model disagree with each other, so a candidate/control difference cannot be attributed to the candidate. Not a candidate defect and not scorable; the exact-locality gate needs a runtime and checkpoint that are reproducible.

workload_coverage.why: Section 44 weights batch 1 at 0.40 and concurrency at 0.60. An arm that was not run is left out of the matrix rather than filled in, and the weights that remain are renormalised by decide.py - so a partial run is reported as a partial verdict instead of a full one with invented halves.

the_configuration_trade_off: The candidate holds budget_fraction 1.00 and hit_ratio 1.00, which the batch-1 axis sweeps resolved as best there (+1.63% against +1.26% at the defaults). At concurrency the same settings are WORSE than the defaults: concurrency 4 reads -1.29% here against -0.46% for the shipped configuration on the mode axis. That is the residency story again - a set-aside sized for a footprint that fits costs the weight stream more once it does not - and it means the best configuration is workload-dependent. A planner that picked the set-aside from the measured footprint-to-capacity ratio rather than from a constant is an open item, and this file is the evidence for it.
